texts.preamble: Ajay Sharma @ Bobby vs State Of Haryana on 15 October, 2025 Author: Anoop Chitkara Bench: Anoop Chitkara Crm-M-48270-2025 In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh Crm-M-48270-2025 Reserved on: 01.10.2025 Pronounced on: 15.10.2025 Ajay Sharma @ Bobby ...Petitioner Versus State of Haryana ...Respondent Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Anoop Chitkara
texts.facts: 1. The petitioner incarcerated in the FIR captioned above came before this Court under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, [BNSS], seeking regular bail. 2. In paragraph 6 of the bail petition, the petitioner declares that he has no criminal antecedents. 3. The facts and allegations are being taken from the order dated 14.07.2025 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Kurukshetra, which reads as follows: Ajay Sharma @ Bobby vs State Of Haryana on 15 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101424652/ 1 "Briefly stated, Injured Uday, son of Sanjeev Kumar, is a 4th-year B.A. LL.B. student at Kurukshetra University (KUK) and resides in Room No. B-46 of Tagore Hostel. It is alleged that on the intervening night of 26/27.05.2025, around 12:45-1:00 A.M., he, along with his friend Amandeep, a 2nd-year LL.B. student, proceeded on a Bullet motorcycle bearing registration number HR- 02AY-1664 to get food outside the University premises. During this time, Amandeep received a phone call from their friend Gurnam, a 1 of 7 CRM-M-48270-2025 resident of Amupur, District Karnal, informing them that another friend of Rahul was being harassed by someone in the hostel and that a motorcycle was required to settle the matter. Accordingly, Uday and Amandeep reached outside Devi Lal Hostel within five minutes, where they found Rahul and Rohit, who already had a motorcycle. Subsequently, all five persons went to the first floor of Bhim Hostel, to the room where the alleged miscreants were believed to be staying. However, the room was locked. They then came down to the ground floor, where they found an open room occupied by 6-7 boys from the PHSO group, including Manish Ramgarhia, Krish Jat, Robin Paiga, and Sachin Dhillo, among others. The group appeared to be intoxicated and was creating a disturbance. Upon seeing Uday and Gurnam, the PHSO members began hurling abuses. It is noted that members of the PHSO group had previously assaulted Gurnam Singh a few days prior, though a compromise had reportedly been reached. Uday and his companions requested them to stop the abusive behavior. However, due to the deteriorating situation, Uday left the spot. Gurnam and Rohit also returned to Devi Lal Hostel. Due to the heat, Uday, along with Amandeep and Rahul, proceeded to Gujjar Dharamshala, where they had already booked a room. Meanwhile, when the complainant and Rahul were leaving Devi Lal Hostel, a group of 15-16 masked individuals allegedly led by Manish Ramgarhia, who was unmasked, approached them from Narhari Hostel. They were armed with gandasis and dandas and assaulted the complainant party. Uday stopped his motorcycle inside Devi Lal Hostel. Amandeep and Rahul, who were pillion riders, dismounted and ran toward the hostel stairs to save themselves. Uday also abandoned his motorcycle and ran but slipped due to rainwater on the ground and because he was wearing bathroom slippers. It had rained a day or two earlier, making the area slippery. Thereafter, Manish Ramgarhia attacked Uday's left leg and knee with a gandasi. Robin Paiga struck his right leg with a gandasi, while Krish Jat, Sachin Dhillo, and 8-10 unidentified accomplices attacked his arms and legs with dandas. During the assault, they shouted threats such as, "Today, you are slashed; next will be your friend Gurnam." Uday identified the attackers by their appearance and voices, though he could not identify the remaining assailants. Upon hearing the noise, Uday's friends rushed to the spot, prompting the attackers to flee while issuing further threats. 2 of 7 CRM-M-48270-2025 Uday was taken to LNJP Hospital, Kurukshetra by Gurnam and Amandeep. He was then referred to Kalpana Chawla Medical College, Karnal, but due to safety concerns, his family had him admitted to Singhu Hospital, Jagadhri (Yamunanagar), where his statement was recorded, resulting in the registration of the present FIR." Petitioner's counsel submits that co-accused Sachin has already been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 19.09.2025 passed in CRM-M-40725-2025 and even case of the present petitioner is on better footing as he is not named in the FIR. 5.
texts.arguments: The petitioner's counsel prays for bail by imposing any stringent conditions and contends that further pre-trial incarceration would cause an irreversible injustice to the petitioner and their family. Counsel further submits that the petitioner would have no objection whatsoever to any stringent conditions that this Court may impose, including that if the petitioner repeats the offense or commits any non-bailable offense which provides for a sentence of imprisonment for more than seven years, the State may file an application to revoke this bail before the concerned Court having jurisdiction over this FIR, which shall have the authority to cancel this bail, and may do so at their discretion, to which the petitioner shall have no objection. 6. Counsel for the State as well as complainant, oppose the bail. It is further submitted that the present petitioner along with co-accused had caused grievous injuries to injured with deadly weapons. 10. The law of bail, like any other branch of law, has its own philosophy, and occupies an important place in the administration of justice and the concept of bail emerges from the conflict between the Ajay Sharma @ Bobby vs State Of Haryana on 15 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101424652/ 3 police power to restrict liberty of a man who is alleged to have committed a crime, and presumption of innocence in favour of --Is Article 21 of the Constitution, which is the most basic of all the fundamental rights in our Constitution, not violated in such a case? Personal liberty deprived when bail is refused, is too precious a value of our constitutional system recognised under Art. 21 that the curial power to negate it is a great trust exercisable, not casually, but judicially with lively concern for the cost to the individual and the community.4 Supreme Court of India in Vaman Narain Ghiya v. state of Rajasthan, [E-SCR] ; [2008] 17 SCR 369, Para 16, decided on 12.12.2008. Before accepting the surety, the concerned Court must be satisfied that if the accused fails to appear, the surety is capable of producing the accused. However, instead of surety, the petitioner may provide a fixed deposit of INR 10,000/-, with a clause that the interest shall not be accumulated in FD, either drawn from a State-owned bank or any bank listed on the National Stock Exchange and/or Bombay Stock Exchange, in favour of the "Chief Judicial Magistrate" of the concerned Sessions Division; or a fixed deposit made in the name of the petitioner, with similar terms and with endorsement from the banker stating that the FD shall not be encumbered or redeemed without the permission of the concerned trial Court, or until the surety bond has been discharged. 15. While furnishing a personal bond, the petitioner shall mention the following personal identification details: 1. AADHAR number 2. Passport number (If available) and when the attesting officer/court considers it appropriate or considers the accused a flight risk. 3. Mobile number (If available) 4. E-Mail id (If available) 16. 17. The petitioner shall abide by all statutory bond conditions and appear before the concerned Court(s) on all dates. The petitioner shall not tamper with the evidence, influence, browbeat, pressurize, induce, threaten, or promise, directly or indirectly, any witnesses, Police officials, or any other person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case or dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Police or the Court. This Court is imposing this condition to rule out any attempt by the accused to incapacitate, influence, or cause any discomfort to the victim. Reference be made to Vikram Singh v Central Bureau of Investigation, 2018 All SCR (Crl.) 458); and Aparna Bhatt v. The State of Madhya Pradesh, 2021:INSC:192, 2021 SCC Online SC 230. 19. Given the background of allegations against the petitioner, it becomes paramount to protect the victim, and their family members, as well as the members of society, and incapacitating the accused would be one of the primary options until the filing of the closure report or discharge, or acquittal. Given the nature of the allegations and the other circumstances peculiar to this case, the 5 Ajay Sharma @ Bobby vs State Of Haryana on 15 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101424652/ 5 of 7 CRM-M-48270-2025 petitioner shall surrender all weapons, firearms, and ammunition, if any, along with the arms license to the concerned authority within fifteen days from release from prison and inform the Investigator about the compliance. Restricting firearms would instill confidence in the victim(s), their families, and society; it would also restrain the accused from influencing the witnesses and repeating the offense. 20. The conditions mentioned above imposed by this court are to endeavor to reform and ensure the accused does not repeat the offense. In Mohammed Zubair v. State of NCT of Delhi, 2022:INSC:735 [Para 28], Writ Petition (Criminal) No 279 of 2022, Para 29, decided on July 20, 2022, A Three-Judge bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court holds that "The bail conditions imposed by the Court must not only have a nexus to the purpose that they seek to serve but must also be proportional to the purpose of imposing them. The courts, while imposing bail conditions must balance the liberty of the accused and the necessity of a fair trial. While doing so, conditions that would result in the deprivation of rights and liberties must be eschewed." 21. It is clarified that if the petitioner violates any bail condition, the State and/or the victim may file an application for bail cancellation before the trial court, which shall be competent to cancel the bail or add more conditions. 22. The significant consideration for granting bail is that the Court aims to give the petitioner another chance to course-correct, reform, and reintegrate into the community as an ideal citizen. To ensure that the petitioner also abides by the assurance made on the petitioner's behalf by not repeating the offence or indulging in any crime, it shall be desirable to impose the following additional condition. 23. This bail is conditional, with the foundational condition being that if the petitioner repeats the offense or commits any non-bailable offense which provides for a sentence of imprisonment for more than seven years, the State shall file an application to revoke this bail before the concerned Court having jurisdiction over this FIR, which shall have the authority to cancel this bail, and as per their discretion, they may cancel this bail. 24. 25. In Amit Rana v. State of Haryana, CRM-18469-2025 [Decided on 05.08.2025), in CRA-D-123-2020], a Division Bench of Punjab and Haryana High Court in paragraph 13, holds that "To ensure that every person in judicial custody who has been granted bail or whose sentence has been suspended gets back their liberty without any delay, it is 6 of 7 CRM-M-48270-2025 appropriate that whenever the bail order or the orders of suspension of sentence are not immediately sent by the Registry, computer systems, or Public Prosecutor, then in such a situation, to facilitate the immediate restoration of the [LEAKAGE_MASK] by any Court, the downloaded copies of Ajay Sharma @ Bobby vs State Of Haryana on 15 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101424652/ 6
